literal: Family and ease (from an old classical greeting meaning 'you have come to family and trodden level ground')
usage: This is the standard, ubiquitous greeting for welcoming someone to your home, country, or business. It is used across all Levantine regions and is appropriate for both formal and informal situations. It is often shortened to just 'ahlan' in casual contexts.

variants.label: to a man
variants.note: Add the preposition 'feek' to specifically address a single male guest.

variants.label: to a woman
variants.note: Add the preposition 'feeki' to specifically address a single female guest.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Used when welcoming multiple people at once.

variants.label: shortened / casual
variants.note: Used as a quick, casual welcome or as a general greeting equivalent to 'hello'.

variants.label: very warm / exaggerated
variants.note: Used to show extreme hospitality and warmth, especially common in Syria and Lebanon.

responses.english: Welcome to you too (replying to a man)
Welcome to you too (replying to a woman)
Welcome to you too (replying to a group)

examples.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan feekom bbeitna, tfaddalo.
examples.english: Welcome to our home, please come in.

examples.transliteration: ya meet ahlan wa sahlan, nawwarto!
examples.english: A hundred welcomes, you brought light to the place!

examples.arabic: أَهْلاً وَسَهْلاً فِيك بِلُبْنَان، إِنْ شَاءَ الله تِنْبِسِط.
examples.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan feek blibnan, inshallah tinbisit.
examples.english: Welcome to Lebanon, hopefully you will enjoy yourself.
